title: Newspaper Incitement To Offences Act 1908
definition: A repressive legislative measure enacted by the British colonial government to empower magistrates to confiscate printing presses and property used for publishing material deemed to incite murder or acts of violence.
importanceInUpsc: Essential for understanding the evolution of colonial press censorship, the suppression of the Swadeshi movement, and the trajectory of Indian nationalism.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Newspaper Incitement To Offences Act 1908.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
